title: Barbell Abdominal Rollouts
instructions: Load a barbell with round plates and place it on the floor.
Kneel behind the bar and grip it with both hands, shoulder-width apart.
Position your shoulders over the bar and engage your core.
Slowly roll the barbell forward, extending your body as far as you can without arching your lower back.
Pause briefly at the extended position, keeping your core tight.
Pull the barbell back toward your knees by contracting your abs, returning to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of reps, maintaining control throughout.
tips: Keep your hips from sagging - a tight core prevents lower back strain.
Move slowly and with control during both the rollout and return to avoid using momentum.
Squeeze your glutes to help stabilize your hips throughout the movement.
Keep your arms straight and avoid bending at the elbows.
Exhale as you pull the barbell back in to engage your core more deeply.
Use a padded surface or mat under your knees to reduce discomfort during the exercise.
Start with partial rollouts by only rolling the bar out halfway until you build enough core strength for the full range.
Add a pause at full extension to increase time under tension and core engagement.
Roll out from a standing position instead of kneeling once you can control the full range from the floor.
Increase rep volume or sets gradually to build endurance without compromising form.
Slow down the tempo. Take 3–5 seconds to roll out and return, emphasizing control.
